liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **The Promised Land** (2 reviews): Mic problems and forgotten lyrics hampered an otherwise groove-driven performance; Weir forgets the words, laughs, and jokes with the crowd, asking what they are laughing at [16][22]
- **When I Paint My Masterpiece** (2 reviews): Reviewer attended this show and liked the second-set Masterpiece coming out of Space; Reviewer dislikes Weir singing this song coming out of Space, preferring Garcia's band versions [14][21]
- **Crazy Fingers** (1 review): Called one of the best versions ever, with a small lyric slip and Garcia's warm, emotional vocal [19]
- **China Doll** (1 review): Reviewer finds this China Doll absolutely gorgeous [19]
- **Space** (1 other source): A ten-second patch in Space comes from an ultramatrix source [2]
- **Throwing Stones** (1 review): The reviewer says the middle jam of this song sums up the show [12]
- **Not Fade Away** (1 other source): A short stretch of this song, 7:31 to 7:37, is supplied from another source [1]

## The recordings

- **gd1987-06-21.sbd.walker-scotton.miller.83767.sbeok.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 21 songs; 158 min; rated 3.43/5 by 7 [1]
- **gd1987-06-21.152599.nak700.severson.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 22 songs; 157 min [2]
- **gd1987-06-21.138261.AKG414.bryant.miller.sirmick.sbeok.flac16**: source not stated; 21 songs; 162 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [5]
- **gd1987-06-21.sbd.painoman.17348.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 21 songs; 149 min; rated 5/5 by 3 [7]. Said about its sound: Reviewer describes the soundboard as rich and creamy, typical of the band's sound in those years; Soundboard has audience patches covering China Doll, Playing In The Band, and into Space [7][19]

## Around the show

- The show began earlier in the day, with views of Berkeley, the Bay, San Francisco and the Golden Gate Bridge [11]
- The concert fell on the twentieth anniversary of the summer of love, which gave it extra meaning for the reviewer [11]
- Weir played the first Watchtower the night before this show during the Greek run [18]
- Setlists in 1987 were dull with short, intense second sets; this show's tight, seamless second set differs [12]
- Reviewer prefers this version to the Ventura one, finding it more alive despite the missing Hammond solo [16]
- Reviewer rates this the best of the three Greek shows, after a high-gear Ventura show the week before [17]
- The Greek shows had short sets, and a Deal into drums was criticized by a journalist [17]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1987-06-21.sbd.walker-scotton.miller.83767.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Cassette Master (TDK MA-XG90/Sony D5) [1]. Also: Chain: AKG 414 microphones, PCM, DAT, Sound Forge, then CD; tapes came from Paul Scotton and Joani Walker [1]
- **gd1987-06-21.152599.nak700.severson.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Mark Severson; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Mark Severson's Master Audience Cassettes; Nakamichi 700 mics > Sony D6M [2]
- **gd1987-06-21.138261.AKG414.bryant.miller.sirmick.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Robert Bryant; transferred by Charlie Miller and SIRMick and Rich Gastwirt; source: Source: AKG 414 B/TL cardioids > ORTF > Oade PS > Sony PCM FI > dat (44.1); Taped by Robert Bryant and provided by Rich Gastwirt; Transfer: Dat > Sony PCM-R500… [5]. Also: AKG 414 recording; this is a new transfer of the same source used in shnid 76379 [5]
- **gd1987-06-21.sbd.painoman.17348.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Painoman; source: SBD>PCM>CASS>DAT>CD [7]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Jerry Garcia: [1987-06-21 Grateful Dead Ticket - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/image/1987-06-21-grateful-dead-ticket/) [24]
